question: Which big banks have live tokenized deposits or deposit tokens?
answer: 4 of the 16 big institutions in the library have tokenized deposits or deposit tokens in use: J.P. Morgan, Citi, BNY and HSBC. The rest are piloting, have announced plans, or show nothing yet. 3 of the 16 are asset managers, not banks.

items.text: J.P. Morgan's deposit tokens are live for institutional clients: Blockchain Deposit Accounts run on J.P. Morgan's private ledger in eight currencies, and the JPMD dollar token runs on Ethereum and Base.

sections.title: Everything each one has built
sections.sub: Each cell gives the status and a one-sentence description. The last column measures scale only; no institution has a published stress or recovery record. On a phone, swipe the table sideways.
columns: Scale (library column 'Scale & recovery'; measures scale only)

rows.note: Institutional clients and named banks use J.P. Morgan's Kinexys blockchain products for payments, financing and tokenization in several regions.
J.P. Morgan issues deposit tokens (JPM Coin / JPMD) and Blockchain Deposit Accounts, which are claims on J.P. Morgan bank deposits, not stablecoins or central-bank money.
Kinexys runs tokenization and fund-flow services and supports J.P. Morgan Asset Management's tokenized money-market funds on public Ethereum.
Kinexys keeps the platform records for specific digital-asset workflows; this is not a general crypto-custody service.
Bank-money payments and financing settle repeatedly on Kinexys; KB Kookmin Bank added a named import-export route, and Project Acacia was a controlled repo trial in Australia.
Kinexys Digital Financing and the Tokenized Collateral Network handle repeat secured-financing and collateral work, which does not make those assets eligible at every clearinghouse.

J.P. Morgan reports large repeat volume on Kinexys (over $4 trillion since inception and over $7 billion a day on average, per its June 29, 2026 release) but no public stress, correction or recovery case.

Institutional clients use existing Citi accounts for Citi Token Services, 24/7 dollar clearing and a live private-share depositary-receipt product; a separate Citi–Coinbase route links bank accounts and stablecoin acceptance.
Citi Token Services moves tokenized Citi deposits between Citi branches around the clock in seven markets and reports billions processed; clients do not hold the tokens themselves.
Citi launched Digital Depositary Receipts on the SIX exchange and completed one first private-share transaction.
Citi acts as custodian only for its own Digital Depositary Receipts; no general crypto-custody service was found.
Citi Token Services and 24/7 dollar clearing run repeat routes in seven markets, and Citi completed live dollar payments with FAB and OCBC on Swift's blockchain ledger (reported Sep 2, 2026).
A Citi paper reports one completed margin payment using digital collateral (client unnamed); other collateral uses are still being developed.
Citi reports repeat use and billions in processed value across seven markets, but no public outage, reversal or recovery case.
Institutional clients use BNY platforms for digital cash, tokenized money-market funds, USDC custody and conversion, and digital fund records.
BNY mirrors participating clients' existing deposits on its own private platform; the ordinary bank deposit stays the legal claim.
BNY links official money-market-fund records to Goldman Sachs's tokenized 'mirror' shares and launched a Digital Transfer Agency for funds whose records live on public blockchains.
BNY runs institutional digital custody, including client USDC wallets, and holds most of the disclosed reserves of SG-FORGE's USD CoinVertible token.
Digital cash, USDC conversion, mirror tokens and digital transfer agency all work inside BNY-connected routes, not across an open multi-bank network.
BNY's mirrored-deposit service started with collateral and margin uses for early institutional clients; no completed transaction was named.
Several bounded live services exist, but there is no public volume, stress or recovery evidence.
Bank of America publishes research on stablecoins and tokenized deposits but offers no digital-asset access product.
Bank of America joined 20 other institutions committing to form a shared stablecoin company and is hiring for stablecoin and tokenized-deposit products; nothing has been issued.
Current job postings show it is building tokenization and digital-asset processing for post-trade work; no tokenized asset has been issued.
No public Bank of America digital-asset custody service was found.
Job postings cover stablecoin settlement, tokenized deposits and blockchain payments; no live service or completed payment was found.
No Bank of America tokenized-collateral transaction was found.
No operating scale or recovery record exists for a Bank of America digital-asset system.
Qualified purchasers can buy the live SWEEP tokenized private liquidity fund (with Galaxy); other platform targets are not live.
State Street's platform roadmap includes tokenized deposits and stablecoins, but no State Street-issued tokenized deposit was found.
State Street Investment Management launched the SWEEP tokenized private liquidity fund and a separate stablecoin-reserves money-market fund.
State Street's production digital-asset platform supports custody and wallet functions, with coverage varying by asset and permission.
SWEEP accepts and pays out stablecoins for subscriptions and redemptions, within product limits.
State Street research and product plans aim to make tokenized money-market funds usable as collateral; no counterparty acceptance was found.
A production platform and two named live funds exist, but no public usage, stress or recovery data.
Institutional investors can reach selected money-market funds through the BNY–Goldman Sachs tokenized route.
Goldman joined the commitment to form a shared stablecoin company aiming at a U.S.-dollar product in the first half of 2027; nothing has been issued.
Goldman's GS DAP platform creates 'mirror' tokens for selected money-market-fund positions, while BNY keeps the official ownership record.
The route relies on BNY and fund custodians; no Goldman digital-asset custody service was found in the reviewed sources.
The live BNY–GS DAP route connects fund subscriptions, official records and mirror-token creation, but it is not general on-chain settlement.
The two firms say the mirror tokens could later be used as collateral; no live use was found.
One named live multi-manager product exists; public volume, stress and recovery evidence is incomplete.
Clients can buy Morgan Stanley-branded Bitcoin, Ether and Solana exchange-traded products; the Bitcoin trust reported more than $381 million in assets in July 2026.
Morgan Stanley publishes research on stablecoins and tokenized deposits but issues no digital money.
Morgan Stanley Investment Management launched exchange-traded products holding Bitcoin, Ether and Solana; these are ordinary securities, not on-chain fund shares.
No Morgan Stanley digital-asset custody service was found; the products use third-party custodians.
Morgan Stanley research models 24/7 digital settlement, but no settled transaction was found.
A Galaxy referral arrangement is designed to swap clients' lent crypto for ETP shares for margin and lending; no completed client transaction was disclosed.
A live product suite reports assets under management, but there is no proprietary rail or stress record.
Select corporate and commercial clients are the planned first users once the tokenized-deposit service starts.
Wells Fargo announced its own tokenized deposits on Aug 4, 2026 for a limited fall 2026 rollout and joined the shared-stablecoin-company commitment; no issuance was found as of Oct 19, 2026.
The annual report mentions tokenization pilots and development for bonds and Treasuries; no live tokenized asset was found.
The platform is designed to support in-house custody wallets in later offerings.
A first U.S.-dollar-to-British-pound route is announced for fall 2026, with more currencies in 2027; no settled payment was found.
Company materials discuss tokenized assets, but no collateral transaction was found.
The announced service has no operating record yet.
Institutional and retail clients use HSBC's tokenized deposit, digital bond, tokenized gold and custody products, which vary by country.
HSBC's tokenized deposit service is live in six markets; its planned Hong Kong-dollar stablecoin, HSBC RedCoin, is licensed but had not been issued as of Oct 19, 2026.
HSBC Orion has supported multibillion-dollar digital-bond issuance, and HSBC runs tokenized gold.
HSBC offers institutional digital-asset custody, with supported assets and legal entities varying by country.
Tokenized-deposit transfers and Orion bond issues recur, and HSBC is in three of the six reported Swift-ledger bank cases (with Standard Chartered, UOB and BNP Paribas/Siemens).
HSBC's products support some bounded collateral uses of tokenized assets and deposits; no clearinghouse eligibility or default case was found.
HSBC discloses repeated issuance, trades and multi-market figures, but no public failure-handling record.
Institutional clients can trade and take delivery of spot Bitcoin and Ether through the bank, with other assets through group companies.

Stablecoin access and digital-cash work run through named group and partner routes; Anchorpoint, a joint venture backed by Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong), holds a Hong Kong stablecoin issuer licence but had not shown issuance.
Libeara and bank services tokenize notes and funds in bounded products.
The bank's own custody service and Zodia Custody serve institutions for crypto and tokenized assets.
Named trading, tokenization and cash routes settle digitally within limits, and Standard Chartered and HSBC reported a live tokenized-deposit transaction on Swift's ledger (Aug 19, 2026).
The Standard Chartered–OKX programme lets named institutions use crypto and tokenized money-market funds held at the bank as off-exchange collateral.
Several live products exist, but public scale, stress and recovery evidence is incomplete.
A custody service for institutional and corporate clients in Germany and Europe is announced; the product page says it starts only after regulatory and technical readiness.
Deutsche Bank takes part in tokenized-deposit and treasury trials and joined the shared-stablecoin-company commitment; no live Deutsche Bank tokenized deposit or stablecoin was found.
Its DAMA 2 blueprint is a tested design for tokenizing and servicing assets on an Ethereum layer-2 network; it is not a recurring product.
Digital-asset custody is designed and planned for 2026, pending regulatory completion, technical readiness and a first client.
Deutsche Bank reports its first euro transaction on Partior after joining as a euro and dollar settlement bank; counterparty and amount were not disclosed.
Research names intraday repo and collateral mobility as leading uses, but no collateral transaction was found.
One bounded Partior transaction is the only operating record; that is not recurring scale.
Issuers, distributors and investors use UBS Tokenize for selected regulated products.
UBS Digital Cash is still in development and a Swiss-franc stablecoin entered sandbox testing in a live environment; no live UBS tokenized deposit or stablecoin was found.
UBS Tokenize issues and services tokenized bonds, funds and structured products repeatedly.
UBS uses its own regulated custody and selected outside custodians inside its tokenized products.
UBS has completed a live repo, bond deals and an in-production tokenized fund subscription and redemption workflow.
A live cross-border repo used a natively issued digital bond and regulated payment tokens.
Several live product types and repeat issues exist, but no public scale or failure-handling evidence.
Institutions, companies and eligible market participants use SG-FORGE's digital securities and e-money tokens, with some countries excluded.

SG-FORGE, a regulated Société Générale subsidiary, issues live euro and U.S.-dollar CoinVertible e-money tokens and publishes daily circulation and reserve data; these are not Société Générale deposits.
SG-FORGE has completed repeated digital-bond and structured-product issues, including a first U.S. digital bond.
SG-FORGE provides issuance and servicing; its reserve page names BNY and Société Générale as reserve holders for the dollar token and Société Générale for the euro token.
A U.S. bond issue on Canton and a Swift-coordinated tokenized-bond lifecycle test have been completed.
CoinVertible tokens are used in some partner financing and decentralized-finance (DeFi) routes.
Repeated issues and daily circulation and reserve data exist, but not route-level volume or failure-handling evidence.
Eligible investors buy live U.S. tokenized funds (such as BUIDL) and European on-chain money-market share classes through named channels.
BlackRock issues no bank deposit or settlement money; a fund share is not money.
BUIDL, registered DLT share classes and European on-chain ICS share classes are live tokenized fund products.
Its digital products run through regulated custodians, transfer agents and platform partners that BlackRock does not all control.
Fund subscriptions, redemptions and approved-wallet transfers work within bounded U.S. and European routes.
Tokenized liquidity funds have named collateral uses with partners; designed features are not proof of wide acceptance.
BlackRock reports large live tokenized-fund scale, but no public stressed-redemption or record-error case.
Retail and institutional investors use Benji apps and portals across supported blockchains.
Franklin issues no bank money; its BENJI fund share is an investment, not a deposit or stablecoin.
The Benji platform uses public blockchains as the official fund ownership record and has operated for five years.
Benji supplies wallets and connects to regulated custody routes.
Peer-to-peer fund-share transfers and stablecoin-to-fund partner routes are live.
Eligible clients can use BENJI fund shares as off-exchange collateral for trading on Binance, held through Ceffu custody.
Franklin reports multi-year operation, material assets and repeat transfers, but no public stress case.
Retail, wealth and institutional clients use Fidelity Crypto and Fidelity Digital Assets for custody and trading, and employers can add a limited Digital Assets Account to workplace plans.
Fidelity Digital Assets, National Association issues the live FIDD stablecoin, redeemable for $1 by eligible clients; it is not an insured bank deposit.
The Fidelity Treasury Digital Fund OnChain class records a secondary copy of ownership on a public blockchain; the transfer agent's book remains the official record.
Fidelity Digital Assets runs repeat custody and trading for institutions and individuals and holds an OCC national trust-bank charter.
FIDD buying, redemption and Ethereum transfers are live, and Fidelity offers real-time and off-exchange settlement inside its custody platform.
Its Collateral Account Suite lets approved outside lenders make cash loans against bitcoin held at Fidelity Digital Assets.
Fidelity runs repeat institutional, retail and stablecoin products with redundant custody sites, but no public outage or stress case.

research.title: How 16 financial giants are going digital
research.answer: Sixteen financial giants are connecting new digital ledgers to existing bank systems. Citi, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and HSBC show the broadest work, but none has proved one joined system working at large scale or through a serious failure.

research.title: SWIFT's blockchain ledger is moving real money
research.answer: Banks report live payments moving over SWIFT's shared ledger, and Oracle now offers banks a way to connect their own tokenized-deposit systems. No bank has yet been named as live on the Oracle connection.
